deed: חברת AIVF הישראלית משפרת בעזרת בינה מלאכותית את סיכויי ההפריה החוץ-גופית
title: Israel's AiVF built a "digital embryologist" that helps choose embryos in in vitro fertilization

trailer.text: AiVF is an Israeli fertility technology company from Tel Aviv, founded in 2018 by embryologist Dr. Daniella Gilboa and fertility expert Prof. Daniel Seidman.
According to Gilboa, only about 23% to 25% of in vitro fertilization treatments end in pregnancy.
The company developed the EMA platform, which combines artificial intelligence, computer vision and large data sets to improve the chances of success.
In 2021 the platform received the European CE mark, and according to Fox News, in 2023 it was in use in Europe, Southeast Asia and South America.
According to Gilboa, traditional treatment requires an average of three to five treatments to achieve pregnancy, and with AIVF the average is 1.6.

glance.label: Founders
glance.value: Dr. Daniella Gilboa and Prof. Daniel Seidman

glance.label: Recognition
glance.value: CE mark in 2021, CB Insights list in 2023

stations.title: Before: repeated treatments and one embryologist facing many embryos

paragraphs.text: According to Ynetnews, only one in four embryos is actually born, and women are forced to return again and again for painful treatments.
According to Gilboa, traditional treatment requires an average of three to five treatments to achieve pregnancy.
She told of a patient who underwent 10 treatment cycles.
Her embryos looked perfect to experts in Israel, yet no pregnancy succeeded.
Prof. Seidman said that traditional embryo evaluation is performed manually, without data and without artificial intelligence.
Genetic testing by biopsy of each embryo can be time-consuming, and can also damage the embryos and prevent them from implanting in the uterus.
Gilboa said that in Israel in vitro fertilization is available to everyone, but in the United States the situation is the opposite.
According to her, 90% of the population there has no access to treatment because of the cost.
According to AiVF's CEO, clinics in the United States can meet only 20% of the demand.

stations.title: The beginning: a doctoral thesis that became a company

paragraphs.text: Gilboa said that the beginning was her doctoral thesis, which became a startup.
According to Maariv, she is an embryologist and biostatistician.
According to Gilboa, in the first stage they taught the artificial intelligence to classify embryos like an embryologist.
According to her, this led in 2018 to an article published in the journal NATURE.
That same year Gilboa and Seidman founded AiVF.
According to Maariv, Seidman is a senior physician at Sheba and Assuta and one of the leading fertility experts in the country.
According to Ynetnews, other experts joined them, including Prof. Shlomo Mashiach and Prof. Dan Ariely.

stations.title: How it works: a five-day video and a score for each embryo

paragraphs.text: The method is based on videos of embryos developing in an incubator over five days.
The videos show the milestones of embryo development.
The technology is called EMA, an acronym for Embryologist Management Assistant.
According to Bizportal, it uses data from clinics in Israel and around the world.
Each embryo receives a numeric score, and the physician or embryologist makes the final decision.
Gilboa said that the system supports decision-making and does not replace doctors.
According to Ynetnews, one million embryo images, 200,000 videos and medical data on 400,000 patients had been collected by then.
According to Calcalist, the company has the largest database of embryo images and patient data in the world.

stations.title: Research: identifying a genetic problem without a biopsy

paragraphs.text: According to Calcalist, a study by AiVF claims that genetic characteristics of embryos can be extracted using computer vision and artificial intelligence.
The study was conducted together with researchers led by Dr. Marcos Meseguer from the IVIRMA clinic in Valencia, Spain.
It was based on 2,500 embryos that had genetic test results.
According to the study, EMA identified significant differences between chromosomally normal embryos and abnormal embryos during the first five days.
The abnormal embryos reached the milestones later.
Gilboa said that the system can determine this automatically and reliably, without an invasive biopsy.
Dr. Meseguer said that genetic test results take several days, and force patients to freeze all their embryos and delay treatment.
The study was presented at the end of June 2021 at the annual conference of the European Society of Human Reproduction and Embryology.
Seidman, who took part in the study, said that the method will totally revolutionize the way in vitro fertilization is performed worldwide.

stations.title: What came of it: approval in Europe and clinics around the world

paragraphs.text: On April 29, 2021, it was reported that the company had received the European CE mark to sell the platform in the European Economic Area.
Gilboa said that about 30% of in vitro fertilization treatments worldwide take place in Europe, and that clinics there have difficulty meeting the demand.
According to her, more than one million treatments are performed there annually in 1,200 clinics.
At that time, clinical trials were underway in the United States in hopes of obtaining FDA approval.
In June 2022, after three years of research and development, the platform was operating in Europe and Asia, according to Globes.
According to what Gilboa told Fox News, AIVF's technology is currently in use in Europe, Southeast Asia and South America.
Maariv reported on a cooperation agreement with Genea Biomedx, a supplier of devices for in vitro fertilization laboratories.
Gilboa said that there are reports of a 30% increase in success rates at clinics.
According to the company's website, Dr. David Walsh of the First IVF clinic in Ireland said that the technology increased pregnancy rates per frozen transfer by up to 30%.
According to the company's website, Dr. Luis Batista of the Perfetto clinic in Brazil reported that embryos with a score of 8.6 or higher implanted at a rate of 65%.
According to Gilboa, with AIVF an average of 1.6 treatments is required.

In 2020 Gilboa cautioned that the improvement of up to threefold attributed to artificial intelligence should not simply be multiplied by the traditional success rate of about 30%, because pregnancy depends heavily on age and other factors.
Dan Ariely said that a woman who knows she will need two cycles rather than four or five can plan a pregnancy better.
On June 22, 2022, the company announced a $25 million funding round led by Insight Partners.
According to Globes, the money was intended to expand the workforce and develop additional digital solutions for fertility treatments.
Jeff Horing of Insight Partners said that the dream of having a child has become more achievable for many.
Prof. Dan Ariely, an expert in behavioral economics, was appointed the company's chief behavioral officer.
The role deals with the impact of the new process on humanity, and especially on women.
Gilboa said that with a digital embryologist it will be easier to set up clinics, and more people will benefit from in vitro fertilization.
On December 19, 2023, according to the company's website, CB Insights selected AIVF for its list of the 50 most promising digital health companies.

stations.title: In wartime: an open forum for patients in Israel

paragraphs.text: Maariv reported that in wartime AIVF set up an expert forum for women in Israel trying to conceive and for in vitro fertilization patients.
The forum was intended for days of uncertainty, confusion and anxiety.
It met online on Mondays at 21:00.
Participation was free of charge and without advance registration.
Ynetnews raised an ethical question: whether the involvement of artificial intelligence in decisions will lead to a generation of children different from those born naturally.
Seidman acknowledged that it is difficult to diversify the ethnic mix in the database, because the technology is expensive and skewed towards the wealthy.
According to Ynetnews, the company plans to add data from Asia, including India, to the database.
Dr. Shahin Ghadir, a fertility specialist in California, said that errors in grading embryos are a possible risk that could affect outcomes.
He also said that embryologists are few and hard to train, so such technology would be welcomed.
In June 2021 the company was still in the process of obtaining FDA approval.

claims.text: ב-22 ביוני 2022 הודיעה AiVF הישראלית על השלמת סבב A בסך 25 מיליון דולר בהובלת Insight Partners.
claims.quote: it has completed a $25 million Series A financing round led by Insight Partners

claims.text: לפי גלובס, החברה תשתמש בכסף שגייסה כדי להרחיב את כוח האדם ולפתח פתרונות דיגיטליים נוספים לטיפולי פוריות.
claims.quote: expand its work force, and develop additional digital fertility care solutions

claims.text: ג'ף הורינג, המנהל השותף ב-Insight Partners, אמר שהחלום להביא ילד לעולם נעשה בר-השגה יותר עבור רבים.
claims.quote: The dream of having a child has become more achievable for many

claims.text: יחד עם אישור ה-CE מינתה החברה את פרופ' דן אריאלי, מומחה לכלכלה התנהגותית, לתפקיד הקצין ההתנהגותי הראשי שלה.
claims.quote: also appointed an expert in the field of behavioral economics, Prof. Dan Ariely, as its new chief behavioral officer

claims.text: דן אריאלי הוא הקצין ההתנהגותי הראשי של החברה, תפקיד שעוסק בהשפעת התהליך החדש על האנושות ובעיקר על נשים.
claims.quote: Ariely is the chief behavioral officer at the company

claims.text: גלבוע אמרה שבעזרת אמבריולוג דיגיטלי אפשר יהיה להקים מרפאות בקלות רבה יותר ושיותר אנשים ייהנו מהפריה חוץ-גופית.
claims.quote: Once you have a digital embryologist, then you could set up clinics much easier

claims.text: במעריב דווח שבזמן מלחמה AIVF הקימה פורום מומחים לנשים המנסות להרות ולמטופלות הפריה חוץ-גופית בישראל, בימים של חוסר ודאות, בלבול וחרדה.
claims.quote: נרתמת למען קהילת מטופלות ה-IVF בישראל בימים אלו של חוסר וודאות, בלבול וחרדה

claims.text: הפורום התכנס און ליין בימי שני בשעה 21:00 ללא עלות וללא צורך בהרשמה מראש.
claims.quote: המפגש הינו ללא עלות כמובן ולא נדרשת הרשמה מראש

claims.text: Ynetnews העלה שאלה אתית: האם מעורבות בינה מלאכותית בקבלת ההחלטות תוביל לדור ילדים שונה מאלה שנולדו באופן טבעי.
claims.quote: Will the involvement of AI in the decision-making process of bringing children into the world lead to a generation of children who are different from those who were born naturally?

claims.text: זיידמן הודה שקשה לגוון את התמהיל האתני במאגר, מפני שהטכנולוגיה יקרה ומוטה לטובת עשירים.
claims.quote: We are trying to diversify the ethnic mix, and this is not easy, since this is a very expensive technology and is skewed towards the wealthy

claims.text: לפי Ynetnews, החברה מתכננת להרחיב את מאגר הנתונים כך שיכלול נתונים מאימהות ועוברים מאסיה, כולל הודו.
claims.quote: the company plans to expand its database to include data from mothers and embryos from Asia, including India.

claims.text: ד״ר שהין גדיר, מומחה פוריות בקליפורניה, ציין כסיכון אפשרי של בינה מלאכותית בהפריה חוץ-גופית טעויות בדירוג עוברים שעלולות להשפיע על התוצאות.
claims.quote: Some of the risks and limitations of artificial intelligence in an IVF setting and laboratory include errors in grading of embryos that could potentially affect outcomes

claims.text: גדיר אמר שמכיוון שאמבריולוגים מעטים וקשים להכשרה, טכנולוגיה כזו תתקבל בברכה.
claims.quote: Since embryologists are very limited and hard to train, this technology would be very welcomed.

claims.text: ביוני 2021 החברה עדיין הייתה בתהליך קבלת אישור FDA.
claims.quote: The company is still in the process of receiving FDA approval.

claims.text: לפי גלובס, מחקר קליני במרפאות באירופה ובארצות הברית מצא שפלטפורמת EMA מהירה פי 50 מאמבריולוג במרפאה ומדויקת ב-48% יותר ממנו.
claims.quote: Clinical research in IVF clinics in Europe and the US found that the EMA platform performs 50 times faster and is 48% more accurate than an embryologist in the clinic.

claims.text: לפי מעריב, על פי נתונים ממרפאות המשתמשות בפתרונות AiVF, שיעור ההריונות גדל ב-48% והזמן שהרופאים מקדישים למטופלות גדל ב-40%.
claims.quote: על פי נתונים שהתקבלו ממרפאות IVF שמשתמשות בפתרונותיה שיעור ההריונות גדל ב-48% והזמן שהרופאים מקדישים למטופלות גדל ב-40%

claims.text: לפי ביזפורטל, בזמן הסבב החברה גייסה סכום כולל של 31 מיליון דולר.
claims.quote: עד כה, החברה גייסה סכום כולל של 31 מיליון דולר

claims.text: לפי מעריב, החברה גייסה מאז הקמתה 34 מיליון דולר מקרן אינסייט, אדם נוימן, פרופ' דן אריאלי ורופאים מובילים בתחום הפריון.
claims.quote: החברה גייסה מהקמתה 34 מיליון דולר מקרן אינסייט, אדם נוימן, פרופ' דן אריאלי, ושורת רופאים מובילים בתחום הפריון

claims.text: לפי Ynetnews, בזמן הכתבה העסיקה AiVF 11 אנשים במשרדיה בתל אביב.
claims.quote: AiVF currently employs 11 people at its offices in Tel Aviv

claims.text: לפי ביזפורטל, בזמן הסבב הפלטפורמה עברה את האישורים הרגולטוריים הנדרשים באירופה, והחברה העסיקה כ-30 עובדים בישראל ובאירופה.
claims.quote: עברה את האישורים הרגולטוריים הנדרשים באירופה. החברה מעסיקה כיום כ-30 עובדים במשרדים בישראל ובאירופה

claims.text: לפי מעריב, בזמן הכתבה AiVF העסיקה 45 עובדים בישראל, בארצות הברית ובאירופה.
claims.quote: AiVF מעסיקה כיום 45 עובדים בישראל, ארה"ב ואירופה ומגייסת עובדים נוספים.

claims.text: לפי ג'רוזלם פוסט, טיפולי הפריה חוץ-גופית בארצות הברית עלו באופן מסורתי כ-20,000 דולר, בכחמישה סבבי טיפול.
claims.quote: in the US traditionally cost around $20,000, with around five rounds of treatment.

claims.text: לפי פוקס ניוז ו-American Society of Reproductive Medicine, מחיר סבב הפריה חוץ-גופית בארצות הברית הוא בממוצע יותר מ-12,000 דולר.
claims.quote: averaging more than $12,000 per session, according to the American Society of Reproductive Medicine

quote_translations.c66: AiVF was founded in 2018 by Daniella Gilboa, an embryologist and biostatistician, and by Prof. Dani Seidman
quote_translations.c67: a senior physician at Sheba and Assuta and one of the most senior and important fertility experts in the country
quote_translations.c73: The technology, called EMA (Embryologist Management Assistant; in Hebrew, Ima, "mother"), uses databases from clinics in Israel and around the world
quote_translations.c64: signed a cooperation agreement with Genea Biomedx, a global supplier of medical devices for in vitro fertilization (IVF) laboratories
quote_translations.c75: is mobilizing for the community of IVF patients in Israel in these days of uncertainty, confusion and anxiety
quote_translations.c76: The meeting is of course free of charge and no advance registration is required
quote_translations.c65: According to data received from IVF clinics using its solutions, the pregnancy rate increased by 48% and the time doctors devote to patients increased by 40%
quote_translations.c72: To date, the company has raised a total of $31 million
quote_translations.c68: Since its founding the company has raised $34 million from the Insight fund, Adam Neumann, Prof. Dan Ariely, and a number of leading doctors in the fertility field
quote_translations.c74: passed the required regulatory approvals in Europe. The company currently employs about 30 employees at offices in Israel and Europe
